adjusted_prescription: When writing SQL queries that combine inner joins with outer joins, it's important to carefully maintain the logic behind grouping and aggregation to ensure your results are accurate. Start by clearly defining how your tables relate and which keys you will group by to preserve meaningful data relationships. Use inner joins when you need matching records from both tables, and outer joins when you want to include all records from one table regardless of matches. When applying aggregate functions like SUM, COUNT, or AVG, make sure the grouping keys are consistent and correctly reflect the data context to prevent misgrouping or inflated results. A helpful approach is to build your query step-by-step, testing each join and aggregation before layering in more complexity. This method ensures you avoid common pitfalls and produce reliable, understandable results when mixing join types in one query.
